newsitem.title: CANADA: Pacalta sees major jump in Ecuador output.
newsitem.headline: Pacalta sees major jump in Ecuador output.

text.p: Pacalta Resources Ltd, spurred by new oil finds on its acreage in Ecuador, expects its 1997 oil production to average more than 15,000 barrels a day, well over six times last year's output, a company executive said on Tuesday.

Based on that production level, Pacalta's 1997 cash flow would be about US$30 million (C$42 million) or US$0.55 cents (C$0.78 cents) a share, company vice-president Bruce Chernoff told Reuters in a telephone interview.

In 1996, the company produced an average of 2,319 barrels a day, most of it from its City Block in Ecuador, and reported cash flow of US$5 million (US$7 million) or US$0.18 cents (C$0.25 cents) a share.
Chernoff's production estimates, which include a 1997 exit rate of 30,000 barrels a day, are conservative compared to those of FirstEnergy Capital Corp analyst Martin Molyneaux.
Molyneaux said in a report on Tuesday he expected Pacalta's exit rates to hit 50,000 barrels a day this year and more than 100,000 barrels a day at the end of 1998.
Pacalta late last week reported results from two exploration wells that lifted the company's stock on the Toronto Stock Exchange by over C$2 on Monday. It closed down 0.50 to 21 on Tuesday.

Pacalta said its Mariann 8 infill well tested at 4,000 barrels a day of 30.2 degree API oil from one of two geological zones. Another well, Dorine 1, hit target depth and logs indicated 60 feet of pay. Production testing was expected to be complete within the next two weeks.
Chernoff said only one zone at a time would be produced at the Mariann location and output from the well was expected to hold steady at 4,000 barrels a day.
"That field is tied in and there's a gathering system in place so it will be a short tie-in to get that well on stream," he said.
Chernoff said Pacalta's continuing success in uncovering prolific producing reserves on its Ecuador acreage keeps surprising the company's staff.
"We've always been very conservative in our expectations of what this whole project might mean," he said.
"We've had some outstanding drilling results that have been well beyond our expectations and have allowed us to accelerate the development."

The company said the first phase of an expansion of its 77 km pipeline system to Ecuador's main pipeline was now slated to be on stream in September after some delays. The project would boost capacity to 25,000 barrels a day.
A second construction phase was expected to be completed by November, allowing throughput of 60,000 barrels a day.

Funding for the initial phase, expected to cost US$11 million, will come from internal sources, including a small part of the proceeds from a US$120 million high-yield note issue last spring, Chernoff said.
The junk bond financing, led by Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette, was rare for a Canadian oil producer.
Chernoff declined to divulge Pacalta's production and cash flow forecasts for 1998 and beyond.

However, the FirstEnergy report, which rated Pacalta as a buy with a 12-month target price of 30.00 and 24-month target of 40.00, pegged average output at 60,500 barrels a day for 1998 and 83,500 barrels a day for 1999.
It also estimated cash flow per share at C$3.45 (US$2.47) in 1998 and C$5.65 (US$4.05) in 1999. ((Jeffrey Jones, Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
